title: Extension and Comprehension
short: A term's extension is the set of things it applies to; its comprehension (intension) is the set of features it implies.
trouble: Learners expect both to grow together. As comprehension grows (dog, then black dog, then small black dog), extension shrinks or stays the same.

blocks.html: A term does two jobs at once. It points to things, and it carries an idea of what those things are like. Traditional logic gives each job a name.

The extension of a term is the set of things it applies to. Its comprehension (also called intension) is the set of features it implies. Add a feature, and the comprehension grows while the extension shrinks or stays the same.

Every feature you add is one more test a thing must pass. "Dog" applies to every dog. "Black dog" applies only to the dogs that also pass the "black" test, so fewer things fit. "Small black dog" adds a third test, and fewer still pass. The tests pile up (comprehension grows) as the crowd that passes them thins out (extension shrinks). If every member already had the feature, the crowd stays the same size, which is why we say "shrinks or stays the same".

blocks.title: Ordering terms
blocks.q: Which has the greatest extension, and which the greatest comprehension: "lemons", "fruits", "citrus fruits"?
steps: Line them up from wide to narrow: fruits → citrus fruits → lemons. Every lemon is a citrus fruit, and every citrus fruit is a fruit.
The widest term applies to the most things: "fruits" has the greatest extension.
The narrowest term carries the most features (fruit, citrus, and lemon): "lemons" has the greatest comprehension.

blocks.title: Thing or feature?
blocks.q: For the term "planet", is "Mars" part of the extension or the comprehension? What about "orbits a star"?
steps: Mars is one of the things the word "planet" applies to: extension.
"Orbits a star" is a feature every planet has: comprehension.
blocks.a: Mars: extension; orbits a star: comprehension

blocks.html: Expecting both to grow together. A richer idea is a narrower idea: as comprehension grows (dog, black dog, small black dog), extension shrinks or stays the same. Check with a picture: each new feature is a smaller circle drawn inside the last one.
